title: PZ Agent Goal Request
description: One goal submission, as `goal.submit` carries it over the Core RPC link and as `pz_goal_submit` accepts it over MCP. A goal is the widest thing anything outside the deterministic core may express — a kind from a closed enum with typed, range-checked parameters — and this object is the only message on the link whose content originated with a language model or a microphone. There is deliberately no free-text field anywhere in it. The answer's goal record is under $defs/record: it travels inside RPC results, never in this slot, and it carries the key's 16-hex-char digest rather than the key, so no encoding of a goal can hand the caller's bytes back out.

idempotency_key.description: Chosen by the caller to make resubmission safe. The channel stores only its digest.

kind.description: The closed set of things a goal may ask for. A transcript or a model's output selects one of these tokens or it selects nothing.

params.description: Typed, range-checked, per-kind. The encoder omits an absent parameter rather than writing null, so every key present carries a value. Which keys a kind requires is the model's business (train_skill needs skill and target_level); the schema states the types and ranges every kind shares.

satisfy_to.description: A fraction of the stat's range, never a percentage.

budget.description: The three bounds that together guarantee a terminal state: wall clock alone lets instantly-failing steps hold the channel, steps alone let one hanging step run forever, and the pending TTL covers a goal admitted and never activated. Omitted entirely when the caller accepts the kind's default budget.

record.description: A goal as the core reports it. Every field, always: the three that may be absent are an explicit null, so a reader can tell 'still running' from 'the peer dropped two keys'. SUCCEEDED requires reason_code POSTCONDITION_MET and at least one evidence key — the honesty rule lives in the record type on both sides, not here.

key_digest.description: Sixteen hex characters over the idempotency key. The raw key never appears in any encoding of a goal.

reason_code.description: A member of the shared protocol ReasonCode enum, or null while the goal is not terminal. Stated by shape rather than enumerated: the set belongs to the protocol layer and is validated there; restating it here would be a second copy that drifts.
